title: Mechanism of State Transitions for the Vector Kuznetsov-Ma Breathers
abstract: We study two types of mechanisms of state transitions for vector Kuznetsov-Ma breathers (KMBs) in the coupled Fokas-Lenells framework on unequal backgrounds. The amplitude imbalance breaks spectral reflection symmetry and generates richer breather morphologies. In the degenerate sector, KMBs approaching a non-self-conjugate degeneration curve from opposite sides yield different limiting solitons, revealing a discontinuous KMB-to-soliton transition. In the nondegenerate sector, the background plane waves become frequency matched at a special wavenumber, converting the KMB into a single- or two-soliton state. We determine the exact transition threshold and characterize how nearby solutions vary with the parameter. We further investigate special limiting mechanisms arising on the self-conjugate degeneration curve and on the real spectrum at the state-transition wavenumber. Numerical excitation provides further evidence for these results.
summary: This paper analyzes how vector Kuznetsov-Ma breathers undergo state transitions within a coupled Fokas-Lenells model. It identifies two key mechanisms: a discontinuous jump in the degenerate regime and a direct conversion to solitons when background frequencies match. The work uses advanced mathematical techniques to map out these transition boundaries.
main_problem: The study investigates the mechanisms governing state transitions for vector Kuznetsov-Ma breathers (KMBs) within the coupled Fokas-Lenells framework.
main_result: Two distinct transition mechanisms are found: a discontinuous KMB-to-soliton jump in the degenerate sector, and a direct conversion to single/two-soliton states when background plane waves become frequency matched in the nondegenerate sector.
method: The analysis employs theoretical techniques including Darboux transformations and spectral eigenvalue calculations, supplemented by numerical excitation for verification.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by vector KMBs governed by a dimensionless Coupled Fokas-Lenells (CFL) system on unequal backgrounds. This framework incorporates intrinsic space–time coupling effects.
key_observables: Breather morphology, the existence and nature of limiting solitons (dark–antidark states), and the transition threshold parameters.
important_parameters:
The background imbalance ($R

main_assumptions: The analysis is confined to the CFL system, and certain limiting procedures (like one-fold Darboux transformations) are utilized to characterize transitions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate KMB morphology maps showing transition curves ($C_{st}, C_{nscd}$), and visualize the resulting dark–antidark or multi-soliton states in different regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the state transitions by first examining the degenerate sector (leading to discontinuous jumps) and then analyzing the nondegenerate sector (where frequency matching causes direct soliton conversion). Special attention is paid to limiting behavior on self-conjugate curves.
why_interesting: While focused on nonlinear PDEs, the study of stable/unstable localized structures, symmetry breaking, and transition dynamics shares conceptual overlap with understanding excitation modes in complex quantum systems or optical lattices.
